items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was the place where Roy Eldridge and Benny Carter and everybody that’s come to town, they always end up over there...

ctx.x: [What was your favorite place where musicians congregated?]

For after-hours, just for drinking, Birdlong’s. Everybody went to Birdlong’s. Then there was a place called The Elks, which was a long – must be a hundred flight of stairs up to the top. This is where Eddie Randle’s band played. That’s the band that Miles played with, and the band that Miles played in when I first heard him play professionally, the first time, after I went over – Duke took me over to his school – Buchanan – to meet Miles. Shortly after that, Miles came down to Carbondale, Illinois, where I was…
[What was the situation with the union?]

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: I heard some records last night that they were playing on (?), it was Clark Terry and the boy that died...the trumpet player that died...

ctx.x: What did you like about him? Speed?

Yeah. He could get over his horn, man, and I dug that, you know. The things he played. I mean, he didn't just get over. You know, I heard some records last night that they were playing on (?), it was Clark Terry and the boy that died...the trumpet player that died...
